# AI interfaces

> Case studies and measurements on user interfaces designed, built, changed or checked with AI: what was measured, against whom (people, automated checkers or a model judge), what worked, what failed, and which part AI did versus rule-based tools and people. Lessons drawn from them by aspect.

Unofficial; company names describe the subject only. The collection measures; it never says which look is better: taste stays with a person. A lesson's "Checked against people" tag says what checked its evidence: people (yes), people for part of it (partly), only deterministic checks (checker), only model judges or simulated users (model), or only the author's account (none); it hints at how far the lesson travels but is not a filter, so judge each lesson by its own words. Each case says how far its claims can be checked and what stake its author has in the tools: weigh it accordingly; a lesson that rests only on cases whose authors sell the tool is never rated strong, and the maintainer's own projects never count toward a lesson's strength.

With a specific or a new model: process lessons (model ability: no) apply as they are. Start with the lessons tagged yes or partly whose cases name your model or its family in the role you use it for ("By model" in lessons/index.md lists each lesson under the roles the family played in its cases); treat those from other models or roles as things to re-check on yours, not tips. A model released after the newest case (published 2026-11-14) has no evidence here yet. The lessons hold only what the cases show: no prompting advice, and no judgement of which look is better.

"May be outdated" marks a lesson about what models can or cannot do (tagged "Depends on model ability: yes") whose most recent case (the later of its publication date and the end of its work) is more than 12 months older than the newest update in the log: newer models may no longer behave so; re-check it against recent work before you rely on it. Marked now: ACC-1, ACC-2, JDG-2, JDG-7, JDG-8, JDG-9, JDG-10, JDG-11, JDG-12. A lesson's Era gives the years of its cases and the newest model family among them.

<!-- disclosure: generated by scripts/build.mjs -->
Disclosure: the cases and lessons are drafted by Claude, an Anthropic model, and reviewed by the maintainer. At least 5 of the 10 cases involve Claude models or Claude Code, as builders, judges or models under test (studio-go, Agentic audit, Anthropic harness, ArtifactsBench, UW heuristic review); 1 leaves the models unstated. Anthropic is the author or the subject of one case: Anthropic adds a planner and a Playwright grading agent to Claude app builds; by the engineer's account the game maker works where a solo run broke, at over 20x the cost. One case is the maintainer's own project (studio-go, marked maintainer-own): never independent evidence, and never counted toward a lesson's strength.
<!-- /disclosure -->

## How to use

- Before an interface change: run the [checklist](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/checklist.md) (about 11 KB) on the project and change nothing. Each question has a Check to measure (static where no running page is allowed) and cites lesson IDs; its report gives a baseline for every count, so the same counts can be taken after the change. Its measuring notes and the report and record formats are the third file of this route: [docs/applying-lessons.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/docs/applying-lessons.md) (about 18 KB). Open only the lessons and cases behind a gap.
- Learning from the lessons (how a project's agents build, change and check its interface): follow [docs/applying-lessons.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/docs/applying-lessons.md), which uses the lessons route below; its revisit section serves both routes.
- Lessons, one route: read [lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/evidence.md) (about 14 KB, the only file besides llms-full.txt that lists every lesson: one line each with tags, strength, cases and the cases against), then open an aspect page only for the lessons you use.
- Open a case only when you need its detail. Each has "Who did what", "How it was checked", a Numbers table with the basis of each number, "What went wrong" and "Practices to copy". File format: [docs/format.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/docs/format.md).
- Once a prediction has met a real event (a change measured before and after, a problem a lesson foresaw or missed): tell what the questions and lessons foresaw and what they missed in a field report ([how](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/docs/field-reports.md)); show the user the exact text before posting.
- Revisit: the newest update is "2026-11-15 — outside review fixes". For each [log.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/log.md) entry newer than your record's, read changes/<entry>.md (newest: [2026-11-15-outside-review-fixes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/changes/2026-11-15-outside-review-fixes.md)), the lesson IDs and questions it added, changed or removed.
- Relative links inside these files resolve against the raw URL of the file that holds them (under https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/).

## Lessons

The aspect pages (tag counts per page: [lessons/index.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/index.md)). Choose lessons in [lessons/evidence.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/evidence.md) first; open a page only for the lessons you use.

- [Build loops](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/build-loops.md): 8 lessons, BLD-n. How agents that build, review or fix an interface were set up to check their own work (a separate grading agent, a reviewer and a fixer, a checker's findings fed back, written criteria): what each part caught or missed, what it cost, and when the work must stop and go to people.
- [Accessibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/accessibility.md): 15 lessons, ACC-n. When a language model or an agent writes, fixes or audits an interface for accessibility: what it catches next to a rule checker such as axe and next to expert audits, what its fixes leave behind or break, how its results were counted, and where people stay in the loop.
- [Model judges](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/model-judges.md): 13 lessons, JDG-n. When a language model scores, rates or reviews interfaces in place of people (a judge for a benchmark, a rater of screens, a heuristic reviewer, a grader inside a build loop), what it needs to see, how its agreement with people was measured, and where that measurement stops.
- [Simulated users](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/simulated-users.md): 4 lessons, SIM-n. What happens when a language model walks an interface in a person's place (a walkthrough, a think-aloud, a usability test), and how its path, its doubts and its ratings compare with those of real people on the same tasks.
- [Measuring jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/lessons/measuring-jobs.md): 6 lessons, JOB-n. How the cost of a user's jobs (screens, clicks, steps, fields typed) was counted before and after a change made with AI, and what rule checks on single pages miss.

## Cases

- [The case index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/index.md): 10 cases, one line each from its front matter (case type, the interface, what AI did, what was measured and against whom, the sample, evidence, the author's stake, cost, a summary). Read it to choose cases; open only the cases you need.

## Optional

- [Everything in one file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/llms-full.txt): the single opt-in file that holds everything (every lesson with its sub-items, every case line, the checklist), for tools that cannot follow links. About 65 KB (~17k tokens): otherwise follow the route above.
- [Update log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ntroccoli/ai-interfaces/main/log.md): what each update covered and changed, and why.
